::: {.callout-important}
## Computer required during the course

Every student must bring a Windows, macOS or Linux laptop to every session with the tools required for the current module installed and working. Only R, RStudio Desktop, Quarto and the starting R packages are required for the first session.

A stable Internet connection is required. If an organization manages the computer, confirm before class that you are allowed to install software.
:::

## What must work {#expected-result}

Before the first session:

- RStudio starts and the Console calculates `1 + 1`;
- RStudio opens a `.qmd` file;
- the `Render` button produces an HTML file without an error.

Before Module 2:

- a path appears beside `Git executable` under `Tools > Global Options > Git/SVN`;
- your GitHub account exists and its email address is verified;
- the [SSH connection page](autre_materiel/connexion-ssh-github-rstudio.qmd) confirms your own GitHub username.

## Installation order {#installation-order}

### 1. Install R

Download R from the [Comprehensive R Archive Network](https://cran.r-project.org/), then choose your system:

- [R for Windows](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/)
- [R for macOS](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/)
- [R for Linux](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/linux/)

Open the downloaded file and accept the default options.

### 2. Install RStudio Desktop

1. Open the [RStudio Desktop download page](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
2. Download the free version for your computer.
3. Open the downloaded file and complete the installation.
4. Open RStudio.

In the Console tab, run:

```r
R.version.string
1 + 1
```

The first result must display an R version and the second must display `2`.

### 3. Check Quarto with the Render button

Recent versions of RStudio Desktop include Quarto. To check that it works:

1. In RStudio, click `File > New File > Quarto Document`.
2. Choose the `HTML` format.
3. Click `Create`.
4. Save the file.
5. Click the `Render` button above the document.

If an HTML page opens without an error, Quarto works. If RStudio does not offer `Quarto Document`, install Quarto from its [official page](https://quarto.org/docs/download/), then close and reopen RStudio.

### 4. Install and check Git {.tabset}

#### Windows

Download [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win), open the installer, and keep the default choices.

#### macOS

Download Git from the [official macOS page](https://git-scm.com/download/mac) and follow the installation option offered for your system version.

#### Linux

Follow the [official procedure for your distribution](https://git-scm.com/download/linux). Ask for help if installation requires administrator rights.

#### Check inside RStudio

1. Close RStudio completely after installing Git.
2. Reopen RStudio.
3. Click `Tools > Global Options > Git/SVN`.
4. Confirm that a path appears under `Git executable`.

If the path is present, RStudio recognizes Git.

## Prepare GitHub for Module 2

### 5. Create and verify the GitHub account

Create a free personal account using the [official GitHub procedure](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/start-your-journey/creating-an-account-on-github). Complete the email verification and write down your exact GitHub username.

### 6. Record your name for commits

Complete this step once in the RStudio Console. Replace the examples with your name and an email address associated with your GitHub account:

```r
if (!requireNamespace("usethis", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("usethis")
}

usethis::use_git_config(
  user.name = "First Last",
  user.email = "address-linked-to-github@example.com"
)
```

This information will be associated with your commits. You may use the private email address provided by GitHub if you do not want your personal address displayed in your commits.

### 7. Connect GitHub to RStudio with SSH

Open the dedicated page and follow its buttons in order:

[Connect GitHub to RStudio with SSH](autre_materiel/connexion-ssh-github-rstudio.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

This page explains how to create the key from `Tools > Global Options > Git/SVN`, add it to GitHub, check the connection, and clone the course repository.

## Install the starting R packages {#r-packages}

Run the following block in the RStudio Console. It installs only missing packages:

```r
required_packages <- c(
  "tidyverse", "knitr", "rmarkdown", "remotes", "usethis"
)

installed_packages <- rownames(installed.packages())
missing_packages <- setdiff(required_packages, installed_packages)

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(missing_packages)
}

if (!requireNamespace("UlavalSSD", quietly = TRUE)) {
  remotes::install_github("AurelienNicosiaULaval/UlavalSSD")
}
```

Then check:

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(UlavalSSD)

dim(UlavalSSD::MeteoQuebec)
```

The result must display two numbers, the number of rows and the number of columns.

## Final test with a Quarto document {#final-test}

1. In RStudio, choose `File > New File > Quarto Document`.
2. Create an HTML document.
3. Save it as `installation-test.qmd`.
4. In an R code block, enter the following code:

```r
library(tidyverse)

results <- tibble(
  value = 1:3,
  square = value^2
)

results
```

5. Click `Render`.

The installation is ready when the HTML file opens without an error and the `square` column contains 1, 4 and 9.

## Check before Module 2

1. Open the [SSH connection page](autre_materiel/connexion-ssh-github-rstudio.qmd).
2. Follow the steps until the message displays your GitHub username.
3. Accept the invitation to the course repository or organization.
4. Clone your repository with `File > New Project > Version Control > Git`.

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| Symptom | Check using menus | Most likely correction |
|---|---|---|
| RStudio opens, but R does not start | Check whether the Console displays an R version at startup | Install R before RStudio, then restart RStudio. |
| The `Render` button is missing | Confirm that the open file ends in `.qmd` | Install Quarto, then close and reopen RStudio. |
| The `Git executable` field is empty | Open `Tools > Global Options > Git/SVN` | Install Git, then close and reopen RStudio. |
| The GitHub connection is denied | Open the [SSH page](autre_materiel/connexion-ssh-github-rstudio.qmd#ssh-troubleshooting) | Check the public key and the GitHub account being used. |
| A package is missing | Open the `Packages` tab and search for its name | Install the package in the Console, then add the correct `library()` to the `.qmd` file. |
| The document works line by line, but not with `Render` | Click `Session > Restart R`, then `Render` | Add every required `library()` and object-creation step to the document. |

If the problem continues, keep the complete error message and a screenshot of the step where the problem appears. Never send a password, access token, or private SSH key.
